title: Placement refusal on the Place_Release fast path is silently dropped — no reject-toast, unlike commit_draw in the same diff
detail: A .Box_Piece_Exhausted placement (empty tier armed — Arm_Placement never checks stock; the tray only dims) is a silent no-op: no last_reject, no toast. The placement half of the economy never teaches by consequence.
recommended_fix: Add the same else branch as commit_draw: on err != .None set inp.last_reject = err and inp.reject_tick = inp.tick so a refused placement surfaces on the toast channel.

title: Pre-commit validity surfaces (R3 route preview, placement ghost) check topology legality only — they can bless commands the Box refuses
detail: Both validity signals derive from topology_apply_edit/validate_place alone. Box-on, the commit authority additionally demands spool stock and a held piece, so the ghost/glow can show a legal move whose commit is refused — the preview no longer predicts the commit it claims to mirror.
recommended_fix: Route the preview/ghost through the material leg too (box_validate against the live run state), or dim/qualify the glow when the matching spool/piece cannot afford the candidate.

title: Box validates before the topology: a too-long draw reports .Box_Spool_Exhausted instead of .Span_Exceeds_Tier when the spool is short
detail: A priceable draw whose span exceeds the tier max_span gets the material error whenever stock < span. The toast tells the player to demolish for tiles — a fix that cannot make an over-max-span draw succeed; the canonical span error never surfaces.
recommended_fix: Check span against cat.pipe_tiers[c.tier].max_span in box_validate's Draw_Pipe case (or defer the spool check until after topology validation) so the topology's span error wins.
